newsitem.title: UK: London insurance market confirms electronic plans.
newsitem.headline: London insurance market confirms electronic plans.

text.p: Four bodies representing the London insurance market on Monday reaffirmed their commitment to its troubled electronic trading system in a bid to end speculation over its future.

A statement issued jointly by Lloyd's of London, the Institute of London Underwriters, the London International Insurance and Reinsurance Market Association and the Lloyd's Insurance Brokers Council said the market's Electronic Placing Support (EPS) system would not be jeopardised by the World Insurance Network (WIN), a project being developed by leading global insurance brokers.

"There has been much speculation over recent months about the future direction of EPS in the London market. In addition, the formation of WIN has given rise to uncertainty as to how EPS and WIN will co-exist, and the recently announced changes to EPS have raised concerns regarding the need for further investment at this time," the statement said.

"We recognise that EPS has not met market expectations and that elements of its current design may not be appropriate for certain risks. However, EPS provides an important first step for the development of electronic commerce."
"We remain committed to using EPS in the London market for those areas of business where practitioners can foresee achievable benefit," it said.
The EPS concept was introduced in the early 1990s but was beset with problems from the start. A timetable developed to introduce its usage was scrapped.
The insurance industry has been slow to take full advantage of modern technology. EPS was developed as a way of handling policies electronically in a bid to cut high administration costs.

Lloyd's chairman David Rowland is among those who have pointed out that Lloyd's and the London market need to become more efficient. A report commissioned by the London market associations from Coopers & Lybrand last year concluded that as much as 300 million stg a year could be saved.
In October last year the WIN project was announced by a consortium of the 'big six' insurance brokers - Marsh & McLennan, Sedgwick, Willis Corroon, Alexander & Alexander, Aon and Johnson & Higgins.

It aims to provide an international and inter-company communication system for the insurance industry. So far no product has been released, but WIN says it hopes to have a pilot project in place by the end of the year.
